name: diff
description: Compares files line by line and reports the differences; also compares directories recursively.

flags.description: Unified format (with context lines) — the standard for patches.
Report only whether files differ, not how.

examples.explanation: Line 5 changed: the old file had timeout 30, the new file has timeout 60.
Unified output: - lines are in FILE1 only, + lines are in FILE2 only. This is the format used by git diff and patch.

examples.output:
Files dir1/app.js and dir2/app.js differ
Only in dir2: extra.txt
examples.explanation: Quick recursive check of two directory trees: which files differ and which exist on only one side.

about: diff output uses change commands: l#c# means lines replaced, #a# lines appended, #d# lines deleted. Unified format (-u) wraps changes with context and is what patch and git consume. diff can also produce a full patch with diff -ruN old new > changes.patch.
useCases: Compare configuration files before and after edits.
Verify directory copies or backups with diff -r.
mistakes: Reading normal diff output when -u is far more readable.
Comparing binary files with plain diff — use cmp or checksums instead.
